extractionNotes: Document structure differs from Biomedical Science's recurring-sub-strand pattern: each of the 4 Strands has exactly 3 Sub-Strands, and each Sub-Strand appears in ONLY ONE Year (not recurring across all three years under a shared name) -- confirmed against the 'Aviation and Aerospace Engineering Summary' Scope and Sequence table (PDF page 20, printed page '20 | AVIATION AND AEROSPACE ENGINEERING') and by summing all extracted Content Standards/Learning Outcomes/Learning Indicators below: Year 1 = 9 CS/9 LO/20 LI, Year 2 = 8 CS/8 LO/18 LI, Year 3 = 11 CS/11 LO/23 LI; grand total 28 CS / 28 LO / 61 LI, matching the prior inventory pass and the document's own printed 'Overall Totals (SHS 1-3)' block exactly.

This exact GESI/SEL/National-Core-Values guidance block (or a near-verbatim variant differing only in trivial word order, e.g. 'at home and in society' vs 'in home and in society') is reused, essentially unchanged, under EVERY Learning Outcome examined across all 4 Strands and all 3 Years of this document (confirmed by direct sampling across Strand 1/2/3/4, Year 1/2/3). It reads as generic Home-Economics-style stock text (it repeatedly references 'home management', 'maintenance of the home', 'management of the home') rather than being written for Aviation and Aerospace Engineering, and the National Core Values list (Tolerance, Friendliness, Open-mindedness, Patience, Hard work, Humility) is likewise identical for every single Learning Outcome sampled. This is the SAME copy-paste issue already flagged in the inventory for 1.1.1.LO.1/LO.2, but it is NOT confined to those two -- it recurs pervasively and is not subject-specific anywhere in the document. Preserved verbatim per Learning Outcome (not corrected); reviewStatus NEEDS_REVIEW set on every Learning Outcome carrying this text. Scope confirmed widespread: sampled and found identical/near-identical in Strand 1 (Sub-Strands 1,2,3 / Years 1,2,3), Strand 2, Strand 3, and Strand 4, i.e. it is NOT confined to 1.1.1.LO.1/1.1.1.LO.2 as originally flagged in the inventory -- it is the standing GESI/SEL/National-Core-Values text for essentially every Learning Outcome in the entire curriculum document.

The GESI bullet list under 1.1.1.LO.1 (PDF page 22-23) contains two bullet markers that extract as garbled control characters ("'^Z/Z" and "^ZZZZ>") instead of a normal bullet glyph -- an apparent font/glyph decoding fault (same category as the ligature-glyph fault noted in the Biomedical Science extraction), not genuine document content. Normal bullet markers are used in this file's reconstruction of that text rather than the garbled control-character glyphs, consistent with the extraction-tooling-artifact distinction (not a curriculum-content correction) -- the underlying bulleted sentence text itself ('embrace diversity and practice inclusion.') is unaffected and preserved verbatim.

The 'GESI, SEL and Shared National Values' column header is printed with incrementing superscript footnote markers per occurrence (e.g. 'GESI1, SEL2 and Shared National Values', 'GESI3, SEL4...', 'GESI5, SEL6...'), consistent with the same footnote-numbering convention observed in the Biomedical Science extraction; the footnote target text itself was not printed on the sampled pages. Each Learning Outcome's exact printed header (including its footnote numbers) is preserved verbatim in guidance.gesiSelHeaderSeen.

Teaching and Learning Resources lists are printed as multi-column bullet/word grids that wrap unpredictably across short and tall cells (mirroring the Biomedical Science extraction's TLR-grid finding); item lists were reconstructed conservatively in row-major reading order. A small number of TLR grids contain what appear to be two near-duplicate entries side by side (e.g. Sub-Strand 'Aerodynamics and Propulsion' Content Standard 2.1.2.CS.3 lists both 'Videos of aerospace propulsion systems in operation' and 'Videos of the various aerospace propulsion systems in operation'); preserved verbatim as two separate printed items rather than merged, since they are not identical strings.

Front matter (PDF pages 1-21, printed pages 1-20): shared SHS boilerplate covering the SHS Curriculum Overview, Philosophy/Vision/Goal/Rationale of Aviation and Aerospace Engineering, 21st Century Skills, GESI, SEL, Learning and Teaching Approaches, UDL, the Bloom's/Webb's DoK assessment framework, the Curriculum Development Panel list, and the Scope-and-Sequence summary table -- not re-extracted per-node per the schema's Phase 5 design notes (document-level context, not curriculum-tree content). The cover-page area (PDF pages 1-2) also contains a garbled title-block artifact leaking fragments of a different subject's ('PHYSICAL AND HEALTH EDUCATION...') front-matter template, consistent with the same shared-template artifact already documented for Physics and Robotics; not part of Aviation and Aerospace Engineering's own content and not extracted.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the evolution of flight.

learningIndicators.description: Trace the evolution of flight prior to powered and controlled flight.
pedagogicalExemplars: Collaborative Learning: In a class discussion, explore learners' experiences with flying objects (balloons, kites, paper aeroplanes) and birds, with the aid of relevant resources.

Building on What Others Say: Brainstorm and build on what others say about humans' attempt to fly like birds; using lighter-than-air-balloons and kites. Organise thoughts using webbing or concept maps.

Experiential Learning/Collaborative Learning: With the aid of a video documentary, textbooks, webpages or any other relevant sources, work in small mixed ability groups to develop posters or Powerpoint presentations on the various phases or stages of flight development. Encourage all learners to participate, respect and tolerate the views of all learners whilst working in groups or in pairs.

dokDescriptions: Level 4 Extended critical thinking and reasoning

learningIndicators.description: Describe the stages that led to the attainment of powered and controlled flight.
pedagogicalExemplars: Collaborative Learning: With the aid of relevant resources, assign learners to work in groups to make presentations on the development of powered and controlled flight. Encourage them to respect and tolerate the views of all learners.

dokDescriptions: Level 4 Extended critical thinking and reasoning

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of safety regulations in the aerospace laboratory.

learningIndicators.description: Explain safety precautions in the laboratory (Aerospace, Physics, Electrical/Electronics).
pedagogicalExemplars: Building on What Others Say: Initiate a question and answer session by asking learners to add to a list of rules and regulations on safety at home.

Talk for Learning: Relate safety rules at home to those in the aerospace laboratory through a class discussion. Through the use of a short video/documentary, learners should identify safety roles in an aerospace lab. Encourage all learners to participate freely.

Experiential Learning: Visit the laboratory where they interact with technicians/assistants; they are introduced to items in the laboratory, as well as the do's and dont's in the laboratory. In the absence of a lab, documentaries/videos should be used. Learners should observe, take notes and present their observations in class.

dokDescriptions: Level 4 Extended critical thinking and reasoning

learningIndicators.description: Discuss the advantages of adhering to safety precautions in the laboratory (Aerospace, Physics, Electrical/Electronics).
pedagogicalExemplars: Building on What Others Say: With the use of think-pair and share, learners identify sources of incidents and accidents and recommend the appropriate solution or precautionary measures. Encourage learners to respect their partners' opinion and agree on what to say before presenting to the class.

Problem-Based Learning: With the aid of case studies of laboratory incidents and accidents, lead learners to assess the effects of not adhering to safety regulations in the laboratory. Use webbing or mind maps to organise learners' thoughts on advantages of adhering to safety regulations in the laboratory based on their experiences at home.

dokDescriptions: Level 4 Extended critical thinking and reasoning

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the balance of forces acting on an aerospace vehicle in flight.

learningIndicators.description: Distinguish between the four major forces (lift, drag, thrust and weight) that act on an aerospace vehicle in flight.
pedagogicalExemplars: Talk for Learning: Building on the basic knowledge students have about forces, teacher goes on to identify the forces of lift, drag, thrust and weight, showing their interrelationship during the flight of aerospace vehicles.

Building on What Others Say: Students draw on their knowledge about forces from Physics lessons to relate forces at work in the environment (e.g., gravitational force, frictional force) to those that act on aircraft.

In pairs, learners go through the process of computing the weight of an aircraft and share with class. Class critique responses of groups in a respectful manner.
